summary.tldr: Bans most promotion of alcoholic beverages and sets out exceptions, enforcement powers and penalties.
what_it_does: Prohibits promoting alcoholic beverages in most ways, including by price ads, testimonials, images tied to lifestyles, or promotions that could appeal to young persons.
Allows some informational promotion and brand-preference promotion in limited settings, such as to named adults, in places where young persons are not allowed, or online with access controls.
Allows point of sale promotions that show only availability or price, and some brand element displays on non-alcoholic items, with limits on youth appeal.
Bans false or misleading alcohol promotions, certain terms or symbols set by regulation, sponsorship uses of brand elements or producer names, and brand names on sports or cultural facilities.
Bans sellers from offering free alcohol, prizes, contests, services, or other inducements tied to buying alcohol, unless an exception applies.

Gives inspectors powers to enter places, including by telecommunication in some cases, examine records, seize items, and order people to stop or start activities; sets offences and fines or jail terms.
summary.background: The bill says its purpose is to protect young persons and others from inducements to consume alcoholic beverages, to protect public health and reduce social costs.
